_meta.indication: Adjunct to diet and exercise to reduce LDL-C in adults with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH)

pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years of age with HeFH diagnosed clinically or genetically
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: percent change from baseline in LDL-C at Week 24 and at the mean of Weeks 22 and 24, compared to placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Treatment effect on percent change in LDL-C at Week 24 was -58.7% (95% CI -65.7, -51.7); p<0.0001

pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years of age with ASCVD or at very high risk for ASCVD with LDL-C ≥70 mg/dL on stable maximally tolerated statin ± ezetimibe
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: percent change from baseline in LDL-C at Week 52 and LDL-C level at the mean of Weeks 50 and 52, compared to placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Treatment effect on percent change in LDL-C at Week 52 was -55.0% (95% CI -59.2, -50.8); p<0.0001

pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years of age with ASCVD or at very high risk for ASCVD with LDL-C ≥70 mg/dL on stable maximally tolerated statin ± ezetimibe
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: percent change from baseline in LDL-C at Week 52 and at the mean of Weeks 50 and 52, compared to placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Treatment effect on percent change in LDL-C at Week 52 was -49.7% (95% CI -54.2, -45.2); p<0.0001

key_safety: Common adverse reactions (≥1%) were injection site reactions, nasopharyngitis, diarrhea, nausea, and peripheral edema. In the pooled hypercholesterolemia trials, injection site reactions occurred in 12% (LIB003) vs 5% (placebo) and nasopharyngitis 15% vs 14%. In the HeFH trial, injection site reactions occurred in 18% vs 3%.
target_moa: PCSK9 inhibitor; a recombinant fusion protein that binds PCSK9, blocking PCSK9-LDLR interaction and preventing LDLR degradation, thereby increasing LDLR-mediated clearance of LDL-C and lowering LDL-C levels
modality: Recombinant fusion protein (PCSK9-binding domain fused to human serum albumin); other

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not convened for this application.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under standard review.

summary.text: Standard-review BLA approved on the basis of substantial evidence from three double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials (004 in HeFH; 005 and 006 in ASCVD/high-risk) demonstrating ~50% or greater LDL-C reduction, a surrogate for cardiovascular risk reduction; approved as a traditional (not accelerated) approval with an advisory committee not convened.

citations.quote: Trial 004 in subjects with HeFH and Trials LIB003-005 (referred to as Trial 005) and -006 (referred to as Trial 006) in subjects with ASCVD or at increased risk for ASCVD events demonstrated LDL-C reduction of 50% or greater in subjects on background LDL-C lowering therapy.

As described in the Benefit/Risk Framework below (Section 2.1), we conclude that the reduction in LDL-C, a surrogate for the reduction in risk for cardiovascular (CV) events, observed with use of LIB003 outweighs the risks when LIB003 is used as recommended in the approved labeling.
An advisory committee meeting was not convened for this application.

requirement.text: PMR 4928-1: Conduct a double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group study followed by an open-label extension to assess efficacy and safety of lerodalcibep in pediatric patients with HeFH aged 6 to less than 18 years.

citations.quote: 4928-1 Conduct a double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group design study followed by an open-label extension to assess the efficacy and safety of Ierodalcibep in pediatric patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) aged 6 years to less than 18 years.

requirement.text: PMC 4928-2: Conduct 'aged' stability studies on at least three commercial or representative lerodalcibep PFS drug product batches stored under long-term conditions for at least 24 months.
